business_scope.primary_industry_name: Leveraged Buyout Acquisition Syndicate and Special Purpose Co

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 10–31 (incorporation, articles, registered office); ss. 101–113 (directors). Alternative federal statute available: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5–20.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Corporate Registry Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) — Form AR-204 / online filing via the Registraire portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital in Quebec. A single subscriber may incorporate with one or more shares at nominal value. No escrow account or capital deposit segregation is mandated for a non-distributing private business corporation; paid-in capital must be fully credited to the corporate bank account before share issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Corporation accept the subscription for 100,000 Class A Common Shares subscribed at CAD 0.01 per share by the Founder Subscriber, and that issuance be recorded upon full payment into the corporate bank account. (2) That the registered office be established at 1000 Rue De La Gauchetière Ouest, Bureau 2400, Montréal, Québec, H3B 4W5, and the Registraire des entreprises be notified accordingly. (3) That [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer until the next annual shareholders meeting. (4) That the President be authorized to execute all banking resolutions, financings, acquisitions, and regulatory filings incidental to the Corporation's private-equity SPV purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation (Clarity and Distinctiveness Review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name declaration (Déclaration de nom) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the proposed French legal name of the SPV (e.g., 'SPV PE No. 2 Inc.') via the Registraire online portal. The Registrar conducts a distinctiveness and confusion review against the Quebec enterprise registry and issued name certificates. Reservation is valid for 120 days; French-language conformity is mandatory under the Charter of the French Language.
required_dossiers: NUANS-like distinctiveness search report generated by the Registrar
Authorization letter from the founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or non-conformity, file a rectified declaration or select a second proposed name; request a formal administrative review by the Registrar within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office de la publicité des droits (Commercial Registry Deposit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in French on the prescribed AR-204 template, containing the corporate name, registered office address, share structure (Class A common and Class B preferred for syndicate investors), director count, and any restrictions on share transfers. The incorporator (founder subscriber) must execute the articles in writing; notarization is not statutorily required for standard articles but is recommended where certified copies will be apostilled for cross-border syndicate use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a request for amendment (avis de rejet), correct the stated formal defects on the portal and resubmit the amended articles within the prescribed response window; extend the name reservation if the initial certificate is expiring.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online transaction portal ('Services en ligne')
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed articles, pay the CAD 356 (approx. USD 265) registration fee via wire or credit card, and transmit the filing electronically. Upon successful review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Constitution (certificat de constitution) and assigns the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), effectively constituting the corporation on the filing date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For filing queries, provide a full copy of the executed articles and registry printout within 10 business days; appeal a refusal to the Director of the Registraire under QBCA s. 14 within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office / Corporate Secretary of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting and adopt the First Board Resolution, bylaws, share certificates, and registered office designation. Record the issuance of shares to the Founder Subscriber, open the corporate minute book and share register, and appoint the initial officers. Ensure all records are maintained at the Quebec registered office.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice of organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance defect surfaces, adopt a rectifying board resolution and re-issue the defective share certificates; file the corrected registered office notice with the Registrar within 15 days of any change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) and Revenu Québec (Quebec Revenue Agency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation under the federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online, and simultaneously open the Revenu Québec account for QST, corporate income tax, and payroll source deductions if staff are hired. A financial institution account in the corporate name is required before drawing the syndicated loan wire.
required_dossiers: Revenu Québec LM-2Q account opening form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CRA/Revenu Québec clarification letters with certified copies of incorporation within 30 days; appeal any erroneous assessment within 90 days of the notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Quebec does not require an industrial licensing board authorization for ISIC 6499 (Other Financial Service Activities) / NAICS 525910 (Private Equity); the Registraire des entreprises du Québec governs general incorporation only, and municipal zoning permits office tenancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — exempt financial holding activity; no manufacturing or operational permit required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative office-use SPV without physical facility triggers no EIA review under the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable at SPV level; any future portfolio operating subsidiary must independently obtain sectoral authorizations (wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste) under MELCC permits prior to operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (SIM-2) provided by the building owner for the registered office; structural load compliance with the Québec Construction Code (chapter B-1.1) and occupational workplace clearance under the CNESST for any employed staff at the SPV office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) and Revenu Québec. Corporate registry: Corporations Canada (federal) or Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec enterprise number - NEQ). Digital portals: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec Cliquez Affaires.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act; deliver articles of incorporation; obtain the incorporation number and, for Quebec, the NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec). Step 2 - Apply for the federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; a federally incorporated company is issued a BN automatically. Step 3 - Add CRA program accounts: RC for T2 corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, and RP/RD accounts if payroll or installments are required. Step 4 - Register with Revenu Quebec for QST and provincial payroll accounts; QST registration is aligned with the CRA BN and results in a separate QST number (format 1000-0000-00). Step 5 - For a foreign-owned SPV, provide evidence of foreign incorporation, head office address, and a Quebec agent for service; non-residents carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST and QST if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or where a mandatory registration obligation applies. Step 6 - Maintain the registers and file the annual declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within the prescribed statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no statutory check-the-box regime analogous to U.S. Form 8832; entity classification follows the legal form under its jurisdiction of creation, and a corporation is always an entity-level taxpayer in Canada. Relevant elections available to the PE buyout SPV: (i) GST/HST closely related corporation election under Excise Tax Act section 273 and the parallel QST election under An Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, permitting taxable supplies between a parent and a 90%-or-more owned subsidiary to be made for nil consideration; (ii) associated corporations joint election under Income Tax Act section 256 to allocate the small business limit, generally unavailable to a non-CCPC SPV; (iii) section 216(4) election for a non-resident receiving Canadian rental income; (iv) foreign affiliate and controlled foreign affiliate elections relevant where the Canadian SPV holds non-resident loan or equity investments; and (v) transitional election for grandfathered hybrid mismatch instruments under Income Tax Act sections 18.2 and 18.21 (post-30 June 2022 OECD hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory for new instruments).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST dual value-added tax (VAT system: federal Goods and Services Tax at 5% plus provincial Quebec Sales Tax at 9.5% applied to the GST-inclusive base; effective combined headline rate 14.975%)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold for both GST/HST and QST: registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents carrying on business in Canada may be required to register even below this threshold, and voluntary registration is available. An SPV making only exempt financial supplies (interest, credit, loan administration) will generally not recover input tax credits on acquisition costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec impose no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based continuous transaction controls, and no digital stamping requirement. Electronic invoices in PDF, EDI, XML, or PEPPOL formats are accepted for GST/HST and QST purposes. Canada is deploying the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework based on PEPPOL for business-to-government e-invoicing on a phased voluntary basis; business-to-business e-invoicing is not mandatory. A tax invoice must show the supplier's BN and QST registration number, the date, description, consideration, and applicable tax rates and amounts; exempt financial service invoices have simplified content requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated at 0% GST/QST where the supplier exports the goods at the time of shipment, in accordance with Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, and retains CBSA export declarations, bills of lading, and transport documents evidencing removal from Canada. Services: zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident and not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance (Part V of Schedule VI; equivalent QST provisions). For an ISIC 6499 private equity buyout SPV, loan interest, credit facilitation, guarantee, and loan administration are generally exempt financial supplies rather than zero-rated supplies, meaning no tax is charged and no input tax credits are claimable on related inputs; separate management or advisory fees invoiced to a non-resident fund may qualify for zero-rating if all statutory conditions are met and contemporaneous documentation is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA G49 / Canada Export Reporting System or commercial invoice cross-referenced on the export report)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT MT103 / foreign exchange settlement confirmation

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and payments authority under the Bank of Canada Act; the foreign-exchange administration function is decentralized. Department of Finance Canada sets exchange-control policy, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises authorized banks, and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) administers tax and reporting duties. There is no dedicated FX-control agency or exchange-licensing regime under Canadian law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility under IMF Article VIII; the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. Both current-account and capital-account operations—equity injection, loan drawdown, LBO disbursement, dividend and redemption repatriation—are unrestricted by exchange control. Profit remittance is subject only to a 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on dividends/interest paid to non-residents (treaty-reducible), FINTRAC EFT reporting above CAD 10,000, the Income Tax Act EIFEL limitation capping net interest deductibility at 30% of EBITDA post-2023, and, where the ultimate acquirer is foreign-controlled, Investment Canada Act notification/net-benefit review. No currency rationing, central-bank prior approval, or convertibility certificate exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil—no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation applies to export, service, or investment receipts under Canadian law. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency and in any jurisdiction. The only applicable controls are FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting for cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more and, for controlled goods, Export and Import Permits Act licensing administered by Global Affairs Canada; neither imposes any conversion or surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account & Operational Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account & Operational USD/CAD Account
Operational Account & Syndicated Loan Disbursement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury use. Canada has no e-money institution licence comparable to the UK/EEA EMI regime; offshore digital EMIs cannot take deposits or access the Lynx high-value clearing system unless registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA, in force 30 September 2024, with registration and compliance obligations phased through 2026) and holding a sponsor-bank settlement account at a Schedule I bank. An offshore EMI may serve as a supplemental FX quote or expense-payments node, but Bank Act s. 54 deposit-taking prohibitions, FINTRAC obligations, and OSFI sponsor oversight render it unviable as the SPV's principal clearing bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not statutorily mandatory. FINTRAC's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations permit remote corporate identity verification through the dual-process method (two independent documentary sources; s. 12 PCTMFR) or the financial-institution affiliate method. In commercial practice, however, every Canadian tier-1 bank classifies a PE buyout SPV as Medium_Risk_Enhanced and requires: (i) a live video-conference KYC interview in English or French with at least one director and the senior fund manager; (ii) notarially certified corporate documentation (articles, board and shareholder resolutions, minute book, Registraire des entreprises du Quebec certificate); and (iii) certified passport copies and PEP/sanctions clearance for every 25%-or-more UBO. A remote-only opening without a notary or commissioner-of-oaths verification step is invariably declined.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity—immediate shareholders are offshore feeder funds (Cayman, Delaware, Luxembourg) with dispersed LP ownership below the 25% FINTRAC threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fund-administrator certified ownership chain chart; authenticated LP register and transfer ledger; fund constitutional documents (LPA, private placement memorandum); GP/fund-manager certificate of incumbency and UBO register; written confirmation that no bearer shares or bearer warrants exist; Quebec beneficial-ownership transparency declaration where the SPV meets the large-corporation threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds mismatch—a CAD 25–100M inbound equity commitment arriving shortly after incorporation with no prior banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription and capital-commitment agreements; drawdown notices; audited feeder financial statements for the last two fiscal years; intermediate bank statements tracing committed-capital accumulation; institutional LP side letters and bank references; Canadian fund-counsel legal opinion on drawdown mechanics; compliance-officer sign-off under the fund's AML/CFT program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or politically exposed person nexus—a director or ultimate LP resident in, or linked to, a sanctioned or non-APG jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due-diligence file per individual (certified passports, five-year address history, professional references, fit-and-proper questionnaire); Global Affairs Canada and OSFI consolidated sanctions clearances, including UNSC 1267/1988 and OFAC SDN annexes for USD legs; PEP screening reports; parent-GP comfort letter; for sovereign-wealth funding, a formal representation letter confirming no prohibited or excluded persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominal economic substance / shell profile—newly incorporated SPV with zero financial statements, registered-office service address, and leveraged capital structure above 4.0x.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LBO business plan and executed acquisition term sheet; fully committed debt-syndicate letters; engagement letters of M&A counsel and financial adviser; fairness opinion and target audited financial statements; pro forma capitalization table with equity-injection dates; board-resolution minute book authorizing account opening and acquisition milestones; Quebec employer registration evidence post-closing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity disbursement pattern—same-day SWIFT MT103 releases to multiple target shareholders, including US and EU beneficiaries, following each inbound drawdown.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow closing-mechanics and release-conditions letter; disbursement waterfall spreadsheet mapping each beneficiary to the executed SPA or shareholders' agreement; standardized remittance narratives tying each MT103 to a deal identifier; bank-approved standing beneficiary list confirmed in the KYC interview; internal treasury policy requiring dual-signature release (two authorized signatories, including one senior officer).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: CAD-denominated equity commitments settle through Lynx—Payments Canada's ISO 20022 high-value SWIFT-compatible system—with immediate irrevocable finality at the clearing member. USD commitments route via Fedwire or CHIPS to the bank's US correspondent account and are either held in a USD sub-account or spot-converted to CAD. Verification stack comprises: (i) pre-wire sanctions screening of sender and beneficiary against Global Affairs Canada, OSFI, OFAC (for USD) and UNSC lists; (ii) FINTRAC EFT filing, automatically effected by the bank for every cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; (iii) SWIFT field 50K/59A matching against the pre-verified UBO and LP register; (iv) ISO purpose code 'CAPD' (capital payment) with narrative referencing 'equity contribution per subscription agreement dated [date]'; (v) for commitments above CAD 100M, head-office treasury pre-funding or a segregated CAD liquidity facility agreed in the account mandate, with same-day Lynx settlement after internal compliance release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) CAD payments to Quebec and Canadian sellers and lenders via Lynx, achieving same-day real-time settlement; (2) cross-border purchase-price wires via SWIFT MT103 with an MT202/COV cover leg, executed through the bank's US/EU correspondents under SWIFT GPI tracking, with a 12:00 ET cut-off for same-day value and T+0 settlement in the US afternoon session; (3) syndicated loan drawdowns under the committed term facility via ISO 20022 pacs.008 loan-funding instructions reconciled to the facility agent; (4) residual target trade obligations paid by documentary commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) issued by the Canadian clearing bank, confined to post-closing working-capital flows. The purchase price itself is normally settled through escrow-agent instructions and seller-counsel trust accounts via Lynx rather than by LC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (CAD vs USD/EUR/GBP) under a bilateral ISDA Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank or a Schedule III authorized foreign bank branch

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible for non-CAD-deliverable emerging-market currencies (offshore CNH, INR, KRW, TWD, CLP, BRL) arising from target-group cash flows; market practice does not support NDFs on fully convertible CAD pairs
FX swaps (principal exchange at spot and re-exchange at forward maturity) for managing USD/CAD deployment of committed capital
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) aligning the LBO term loan's USD floating-rate liability with the SPV's CAD functional currency
FX options and zero-cost collars for hedging acquisition-price and earn-out exposures, subject to IFRS hedge-accounting documentation
Multi-currency cash pools (CAD, USD, EUR) maintained at the principal Canadian clearing bank as non-derivative liquidity rails

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (declaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of registration; supplementary updates to registered disclosure must be filed within 15 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CA$45; continued failure triggers notice of default and administrative dissolution/wind-up of the enterprise registration, generally after approximately two years of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA s. 263.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary date of incorporation (or of the last annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CA$250; failure to file for at least one year may lead to dissolution of the federal corporation by Corporations Canada

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T2 return due no later than six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due remittance generally due within three months after year-end for a CCPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, compounded interest and possible prosecution; repeated defaults may trigger administrative enforcement for tax collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CO-17 return due within six months after the fiscal year-end; balance-due generally within three months after year-end for a CCPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus interest and additional penalties of 1% per month up to 12 months; persistent evasion may support administrative collection measures and corporate registry opposition

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for offering/distributing corporations; a non-offering Quebec business corporation is exempt if it has no more than 30 shareholders, paid-up capital not exceeding CA$15M and annual turnover not exceeding CA$20M; shareholders holding at least 10% of the issued shares may nevertheless demand an audit under QBCA. A private (non-public) federal corporation is exempt unless the articles or shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares request one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations in Quebec; CPA Canada Handbook as the governing reference.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Quebec's transparency-register regime, the annual declaration must confirm or update the register of persons with significant control (natural persons owning 25% or more or exercising control in fact). In Quebec, any transfer of shares altering beneficial ownership must be disclosed to RNEQ within 15 days of the change; the annual declaration serves as the yearly confirmation checkpoint and must be completed by an authorized representative.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 - 5,100 (CA$3,000 - 7,000) for a standalone private equity buyout SPV

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal Part I general rate 15% + Quebec provincial general rate 11.5% = combined headline 26.5% on taxable income allocated to Quebec; passive/investment income of a CCPC may attract additional refundable tax of 10.67%, and Part IV tax of 33.33% applies to certain dividends received (refundable on payout).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (reduces federal rate to 9% on first C$500,000 of active business active income) and Quebec small-business rate 3.2% (CCPCs only; generally unavailable to PE buyout SPVs earning property/investment income); inter-corporate dividend deduction (s.112) for dividends received from taxable Canadian companies; M&P deduction (federal rate 13%) not relevant; SR&ED refundable/non-refundable credits not relevant; no Quebec patent-box for financial holdings.
